design_decisions: Five ACs, not six: the deliverable is ONE flow across two sections; the W5 ceiling is 6 and this card stays under it honestly.

Ownership boundary is the block from ## Quick Start up to, NOT including, ## Troubleshooting. Troubleshooting is t70's section and ac4 counts the level-2 headings inside the owned block (=2) to prove the cut sits at the ownership boundary rather than silently pulling t70's rows into the isolation comparison.
ac2 writes its entry-count leg as >= 250 rather than == 250 so that appends by t70/t71 cannot break a replay fence that is otherwise delta-invariant - the WAL 829 self-destructive-literal lesson.

ac5 keeps the hard 250-entry count and the full 3f1cb760... digest because its job is a freeze, not a replay; the appendability table says NO for ac5 rather than pretending otherwise (same disclosure shape as t68 ac5).
ac1 and ac3 read the base README blob by immutable commit sha (0fdde697...) and the live index by literal key, so both survive future appends; ac4 and ac5 are per-card by construction.

Every behavioural claim in the flow is corroborated against a MERGED implementation file (scripts/dev/dev.ts prefixes, FRONTEND_URL; backend/app/scripts/seed_demo.py wipe_demo_data, RNG_SEED, demo-password-123) so the README cannot drift from the code it describes.

The jargon ban (nine internal-pipeline words) is fenced in ac3 with its own negative control instead of relying solely on the stored tests[249] leg, so the card proves the leg bites rather than trusting a stored gate.

The demo seed gets NO requirement id: the plan names REQ-DOC-010 for the quick-start flow and the demo credentials come from operator ruling b34d15c0; inventing a demo-specific id would be a fabricated citation.
Card and mirror carry zero full-form requirement ids (short form only, assembled in prose), and ac5 re-proves the regenerated matrix byte-identical so the card cannot move a coverage row by landing.
The largest fence is 8174 bytes, inside the 8191-byte cmd.exe command-line ceiling; ac3 was trimmed to fit rather than split into a second command, so the one-line dialect holds for all five.
environment_facts: Fences run under WSL bash on the Windows worktree; git metadata reads go through cmd.exe with wslpath -w (the t65 ac1 lesson: never hand a WSL /mnt/c path to a Windows-side tool, and plain git does not resolve from a linked worktree under WSL).
wc -l reports 0 for a CR-only stream, so CR/LF counts are measured with tr -cd | wc -c.

uv is required for the ac5 matrix leg; node for the ac1 manifest leg; python3 for the ac2 index-extraction leg. Each fence refuses with a named reason if its interpreter is missing rather than passing vacuously.
The worktree gitdir holds Windows-formatted paths, so all git write operations in this session went through cmd.exe /c git -C <windows-path>.
